references_named: Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
rationale: The Constraint Validation API is a genuinely apt mechanism: the native, un-styleable validation bubble is the customs official's verdict, delivered in an authority's voice the viewer cannot reword. Concept and execution collapse cleanly (P1): art-status is enacted as a classification imposed from outside, exactly as on the 1926 pier. The Brancusi reference is precise and double-coded (P7) — the casual viewer gets the deadpan joke, the literate viewer knows the bronze never changed. The Appeal button enacts the 1928 ruling rather than narrating it. Distinct from the catalogue: it shares the value/authenticity axis with Hammer Price and Art is Money but uses a mechanism none of them touch, and it answers the 'but is it art' line with a historical case rather than a one-word verdict.
reservations: The SVG of Bird in Space is decorative rather than load-bearing — the work would function identically without it, which slightly weakens the P1 claim that mechanism enacts idea. The Constraint Validation API is also a relatively well-trodden net.art mechanism (cf. native form validation pieces), so novelty sits at the lower end of strong.
revision_suggestion: Consider making the bronze itself the validation target — e.g. an SVG whose geometry is computed from the user's declared description, so the object literally cannot be admitted until the law relents, tightening P1 further.
